sections.h2: Which Chatham County offices bill the tax and value the property?
sections.html:
Two separate offices handle a Chatham County property tax bill. The Board of Assessors sets the value and approves exemptions, while the Tax Commissioner bills, collects and passes the money to each taxing body. The Tax Commissioner states that its office plays no part in setting values or millage rates.

According to the county's 2026 property tax brochure, the Tax Commissioner bills for Chatham County, the Special Service District, the school board, transit, Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Thunderbolt, Tybee Island and Vernonburg. Look at the line items on your own bill to see which of those districts apply to your address.

  • Tax Commissioner: 912-652-7100, tax.chathamcountyga.gov, 222 W. Oglethorpe Ave., 295 Police Memorial Dr. and 1145 Eisenhower Dr., open 8:30am to 5:00pm Monday through Friday.
  • Board of Assessors: 912-652-7271, boa.chathamcountyga.gov, Suite 113 of the Pete Liakakis Government Building at 222 West Oglethorpe Avenue.
  • Mail: Chatham County Tax Commissioner, P. O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412.
  • Satellite tax offices on Wilmington Island Road, US 80 and Georgia Highway 21 see people by appointment only.

sections.h2: What does Chatham County look like from a seller's side?
sections.html:
Chatham County is the northernmost of Georgia's coastal counties. It covers 632 square miles, and 206 of them are water. The Savannah River bounds it on the northeast and the Ogeechee River on the southwest and Tybee Island sits on the Atlantic side. Savannah anchors the county as its seat, with Bloomingdale, Garden City, Pooler, Port Wentworth, Tybee Island, Thunderbolt and Vernonburg making up the rest of the municipalities.

By mid-2025 the county had an estimated 311,855 residents, compared with 295,291 counted in 2020. On the 2020 to 2024 survey the middle value for a home lived in by its owner is $302,700, typical rent runs $1,471 a month, and 56.8% of households own. Builders took out 4,426 permits during 2025.

Interstates 16, 95 and 516 cross the county along with US 17 and US 80, and the whole county falls inside Savannah-Chatham County Public Schools. Savannah State University and the Savannah College of Art and Design are both located in Savannah, and Live Oak Public Libraries serve Chatham, Effingham and Liberty counties.

sections.h2: What are the Chatham County property tax due dates?
sections.html:
Land and buildings are billed in two pieces. June 1 is the deadline for the first piece and November 15 for the second, while business and other personal property is billed once, also due November 15.

Chatham County billing calendar, from the Tax Commissioner's 2026 property tax brochure
BillMailed byDue
Real property, first installmentApril 1June 1
Real property, second installmentSeptember 15November 15
Personal property, one billNot statedNovember 15

Payment can go by mail to the Chatham County Tax Commissioner at P. O. Box 9827, Savannah, GA 31412, online, or in person. Online payment by credit card or eCheck carries convenience fees, and the brochure says eChecks are free. A check or eCheck that comes back unpaid costs 5% of the amount with a $30 minimum, under O.C.G.A. 16-9-20.

Taxes not paid by the due date are delinquent. Interest and penalties follow O.C.G.A. 48-2-40 and 48-2-44, and a delinquent parcel can also carry a tax lien that a title company will want cleared before closing.

sections.h2: How does an owner contest a Chatham County value?
sections.html:
A written challenge is due at the Board of Assessors 45 days after the notice date shown on your Annual Notice of Assessment. That notice, rather than any tax bill, starts the clock. An appeal can argue taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption, and Georgia supplies a uniform appeal form.

On that first written appeal you must name your method. The brochure lists three:

  • Board of Equalization, with a further petition to Superior Court.
  • Arbitration, which requires a certified appraisal submitted within 45 days; the Board of Assessors can accept or reject it, and you may still petition Superior Court.
  • Hearing Officer, open only to non-homestead real property with a fair market value of $500,000 or more, or certain wireless property above $200,000 in total value.

The Board of Assessors says it welcomes recent sales, photographs of similar sold homes, and lease or income figures. It also points out that it measures square footage from the outside perimeter, so a smaller interior living area does not by itself prove an error.

Property returns are filed during the season that opens with the new year and closes April 1, and the forms sit on the Board of Assessors website under Forms. An initial return renews itself every year at the last final value. A taxpayer unhappy with the current figure can file a fresh return declaring a different value, which protects appeal rights if the Board changes the number again. Working farmland can be assessed at 30% of market value instead of the usual 40%, and conservation use land is valued by how it is used today. Each program asks for a covenant to keep the land in that use for at least 10 years.

sections.h2: Which homestead exemptions apply in Chatham County?
sections.html:
The regular homestead exemption removes $12,000 of assessed value from the county levy and $2,000 from the school and state levies. Every homestead exemption requires that you own the house, live in it and claim it as your legal residence as of January 1, which rules out rentals.

  • Stephens-Day and the state floating homestead exemption: the county awards whichever gives the larger saving, then adds other exemptions you qualify for.
  • Special Chatham senior exemption: age 65 by January 1, combined net income of $10,000 or less, $30,000 off county and school assessed value, plus relief from most state assessments.
  • Senior school exemption: age 62, combined net income of $25,000 or less.
  • Disabled veteran exemption: a VA letter showing 100% service-connected disability, with the amount subject to annual change.
  • Year's Support: when a spouse or minor child petitions Probate Court within two years after a death, the court can award tax relief for the year named in the petition.

Bring a Georgia driver's license or ID and a vehicle registration in your name, with matching mailing and homestead addresses. An application that arrives inside the 45 day notice window counts for that year, and a later one waits for the next year. Buying a different home or changing the deed means filing again.

sections.h2: Who pays the Chatham County bill when a house sells?
sections.html:
The seller is billed because Georgia taxes whoever held title when the year began. A sale in March or August does not shift the bill to the buyer, and state revenue guidance rules out any refund for a partial year.

Any split of the year is therefore a private deal struck at the closing table. If the sale lands between the June and November deadlines, the second installment is still open, so ask the closing attorney whether it is paid at the table or credited to the buyer. A delinquent balance belongs in the payoff so the lien does not follow the title.

Your homestead exemption does not travel with the house, so the new owner files again. If the house came to you by inheritance, look again at the Year's Support option above, and ask the Tax Commissioner at 912-652-7100 for a payoff before choosing a closing day.

faqs.q: Do Chatham County owners pay once or twice a year?
faqs.a: Twice for real property. One half is due June 1 and the other November 15, and personal property comes due in a single November 15 payment.

faqs.q: Which Chatham County office answers valuation questions?
faqs.a: The Board of Assessors, at 912-652-7271. The Tax Commissioner at 912-652-7100 takes payments but cannot change a value or a millage rate.

faqs.q: Is there any appeal once the 45 days run out?
faqs.a: Generally no. The deadline counts from the notice date, and the Board of Assessors can tell you whether anything applies to a notice that never reached you.

faqs.q: Does a buyer inherit my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. Whoever filed keeps the exemption, so a purchaser has to apply again at the Board of Assessors with a Georgia license and a matching vehicle registration.

faqs.q: Will I owe tax if I sell in the fall?
faqs.a: Yes, for that year, because you held title in January. If the November installment is still open at closing, the payoff or proration appears on the closing statement.
